title: Polynomial-time query outside DynFO
formal: Is there a polynomial-time Boolean query on finite relational structures that cannot be maintained by first-order update formulas under single-tuple insertions and deletions, with arbitrary fixed-arity auxiliary relations and built-in arithmetic?
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Specify empty-input initialization, auxiliary initialization, uniformity and the allowed arithmetic relations before asserting a separation.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence or universal proposition, or of its logical negation. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. Pending: Specify empty-input initialization, auxiliary initialization, uniformity and the allowed arithmetic relations before asserting a separation.
context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Thomas Schwentick. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. The candidate retains the bibliography and dated caveats from that catalogue; these have not received a comprehensive independent literature review.
why: An unconditional separation would establish a basic expressive limit of dynamic descriptive complexity.

import_provenance.original_statement: Exhibit a polynomial-time computable Boolean query on finite relational structures that cannot be maintained by first-order update formulas under single-tuple insertions and deletions, even with arbitrary fixed-arity auxiliary relations. This is the central lower-bound frontier emphasized by Schwentick, using the standard empty-input initialization and allowing built-in arithmetic.
